title: Generated Wasm resource runtime integration
objective: Connect a generated FLINT opaque-resource backend through the ordinary Sage.js browser package/runtime loader and verify explicit close plus FinalizationRegistry cleanup end to end

oracles: Existing generated Node resource lifecycle and CoWasm FLINT behavior
Sage.js compiled Python resource wrapper explicit-close semantics

handoff.summary: Generated the declared FLINT Dirichlet-group Wasm adapter during the browser package build, linked its C exports into the public Wasm instance, exposed the generated backend and declaration manifest through the ordinary runtime loader, bundled nested generated Python FFI modules and caches with package-aware paths, and added Node plus real-Chromium lifecycle coverage for explicit close and FinalizationRegistry cleanup. Root integration accepted the independently passing package, browser, portable, native, and parallel checks while retaining the unrelated pre-existing SEA fixture failure as an explicit follow-up.
risks: The browser finalizer assertion needs Chromium with --expose-gc; the smoke test searches standard Chromium paths or SAGEJS_CHROMIUM.

The broader pnpm test:sea check is currently red before exercising this package: its existing mpmath.py smoke fixture resolves itself instead of the bundled mpmath package and reports cannot import name 'mp'. No SEA or Python import files are within this lane's claims.
next_steps: Resolve the unrelated SEA mpmath script/package shadowing regression in an integration or Python-runtime lane.
Extend the generated Wasm selection only when additional declaration resources explicitly opt into the Wasm target.
